items.title: LUCI Desktop
items.name: LUCI Desktop
items.summary: Let your AI agents remember what you've seen
items.description: Luci saves your screen history and meeting transcripts locally, so agents like Claude Code, Cursor and Codex can help you find a page you forgot to bookmark or recall a decision from a call. Capture context across apps without setting up a connector for each one. Includes on-device transcription and daily summaries with Microsoft Foundry Local. Free for Mac and Windows.
top_comments: Hi everyone, I'm Runze, one of the makers of Luci. By day I'm juggling a dozen browser tabs, back-to-back calls, shared docs, and product threads — the kind of screen life where your context is constantly somewhere else. That chaos is exactly what led me here. We kept hitting the same wall with AI agents: every conversation starts from zero. You explain the project again, paste the same links again, describe the meeting again. Meanwhile the answer was already on your screen an hour ago. Luci records what happens on your screen, keeps it on your own machine, and makes that history available to the agents you already use. Ask about a meeting you sat through, a post you scrolled past, or a detail buried in a file you opened last week. No connectors, no per-app integrations. Everything stays local. We also integrate with Microsoft's Foundry Local so audio transcription and daily summaries run on your own hardware. If this sounds like your day, I'd like to hear where your agents lose context most often.
I like the idea of letting an AI agent look up relevant context instead of copying it into every new conversation.

the retention and on-disk answers below cover your own data well. the case I'm curious about is other people's: a screen share where a coworker's Slack DMs are visible in the background, or a video call where someone else's face and name are on screen. that's not really "your history" anymore, it's theirs, captured without them opting into anything. is there any redaction or exclusion for windows/apps you don't own the content of, or is the assumption that if it crossed your screen it's fair game to record?

items.title: Vitals 
items.name: Vitals 
items.summary: A Mac activity monitor that thinks in apps, not processes
items.description: Activity Monitor lists a thousand processes, a hundred of them called Google Chrome Helper. Vitals adds every helper to the app that launched it, so you see 60 apps instead of 1,000 processes, each with one figure for memory, CPU, energy, disk and network. It keeps 30 days of history, alerts you when an app misbehaves, finds forgotten dev servers, and shows temperatures, fans and battery. Every readout can sit in your menu bar, arranged your way. Pay once. No subscription, no account.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt 👋

I'm Atta. I make Mac apps on my own, and Vitals is the one I made for myself first.

My Mac would get hot and slow, so I'd open Activity Monitor and find 1,041 processes, 96 of them called "Google Chrome Helper". It never told me the one thing I wanted to know: which app is doing this?

So I built the tool that answers that. Vitals adds every helper to the app that launched it. One row per app, one figure each for memory, CPU, energy, disk, and network. Click the row, and everything about that app is in one place. It keeps 30 days of history, tells you when an app starts misbehaving, and finds the dev servers you forgot were running, grouped by project.

That is also what makes it different. Activity Monitor and the terminal tools show you processes and leave the adding up to you. The menu bar monitors show you how busy your Mac is, with gauges and graphs, but not which app is behind it. Vitals starts from the app, and I built it to feel like one native Mac app, not a dashboard.

Version 1.1 ships today. Every readout can be its own menu bar item; volume and Bluetooth sit beside them, and you arrange the panel and the window the way you like.

Two days ago I put it on X. 800+ people bought it in 72 hours, which I still don't quite believe. It's $5 for the first 1,000 licenses, then $29. One payment, no subscription, no account, and nothing leaves your Mac.

👉 https://vitalsmac.com

I'll be here all day. Tell me what you'd want Vitals to answer next, and what you'd want it to stop doing.
Pay once, no account, menu bar readouts you can arrange yourself. That's my kind of Mac utility. Congrats on the launch! @attacomsian

Congrats on the launch. Recently, my MBP M1 has been noticeably slow, and I was curious to hunt for a tool that can give me a clear picture of what's eating up all that available memory. None matched my expectations except Vitals. A breath of fresh air to the UI that conveys all those important vitals that are needed, especially on a bit of a reasonably old machine.

items.title: LUCI Desktop
items.name: LUCI Desktop
items.summary: Let your AI agents remember what you've seen
items.description: Luci saves your screen history and meeting transcripts locally, so agents like Claude Code, Cursor and Codex can help you find a page you forgot to bookmark or recall a decision from a call. Capture context across apps without setting up a connector for each one. Includes on-device transcription and daily summaries with Microsoft Foundry Local. Free for Mac and Windows.
top_comments: Hi everyone, I'm Runze, one of the makers of Luci. By day I'm juggling a dozen browser tabs, back-to-back calls, shared docs, and product threads — the kind of screen life where your context is constantly somewhere else. That chaos is exactly what led me here. We kept hitting the same wall with AI agents: every conversation starts from zero. You explain the project again, paste the same links again, describe the meeting again. Meanwhile the answer was already on your screen an hour ago. Luci records what happens on your screen, keeps it on your own machine, and makes that history available to the agents you already use. Ask about a meeting you sat through, a post you scrolled past, or a detail buried in a file you opened last week. No connectors, no per-app integrations. Everything stays local. We also integrate with Microsoft's Foundry Local so audio transcription and daily summaries run on your own hardware. If this sounds like your day, I'd like to hear where your agents lose context most often.
I like the idea of letting an AI agent look up relevant context instead of copying it into every new conversation.

the retention and on-disk answers below cover your own data well. the case I'm curious about is other people's: a screen share where a coworker's Slack DMs are visible in the background, or a video call where someone else's face and name are on screen. that's not really "your history" anymore, it's theirs, captured without them opting into anything. is there any redaction or exclusion for windows/apps you don't own the content of, or is the assumption that if it crossed your screen it's fair game to record?

items.title: Vitals 
items.name: Vitals 
items.summary: A Mac activity monitor that thinks in apps, not processes
items.description: Activity Monitor lists a thousand processes, a hundred of them called Google Chrome Helper. Vitals adds every helper to the app that launched it, so you see 60 apps instead of 1,000 processes, each with one figure for memory, CPU, energy, disk and network. It keeps 30 days of history, alerts you when an app misbehaves, finds forgotten dev servers, and shows temperatures, fans and battery. Every readout can sit in your menu bar, arranged your way. Pay once. No subscription, no account.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt 👋

I'm Atta. I make Mac apps on my own, and Vitals is the one I made for myself first.

My Mac would get hot and slow, so I'd open Activity Monitor and find 1,041 processes, 96 of them called "Google Chrome Helper". It never told me the one thing I wanted to know: which app is doing this?

So I built the tool that answers that. Vitals adds every helper to the app that launched it. One row per app, one figure each for memory, CPU, energy, disk, and network. Click the row, and everything about that app is in one place. It keeps 30 days of history, tells you when an app starts misbehaving, and finds the dev servers you forgot were running, grouped by project.

That is also what makes it different. Activity Monitor and the terminal tools show you processes and leave the adding up to you. The menu bar monitors show you how busy your Mac is, with gauges and graphs, but not which app is behind it. Vitals starts from the app, and I built it to feel like one native Mac app, not a dashboard.

Version 1.1 ships today. Every readout can be its own menu bar item; volume and Bluetooth sit beside them, and you arrange the panel and the window the way you like.

Two days ago I put it on X. 800+ people bought it in 72 hours, which I still don't quite believe. It's $5 for the first 1,000 licenses, then $29. One payment, no subscription, no account, and nothing leaves your Mac.

👉 https://vitalsmac.com

I'll be here all day. Tell me what you'd want Vitals to answer next, and what you'd want it to stop doing.
Pay once, no account, menu bar readouts you can arrange yourself. That's my kind of Mac utility. Congrats on the launch! @attacomsian

Congrats on the launch. Recently, my MBP M1 has been noticeably slow, and I was curious to hunt for a tool that can give me a clear picture of what's eating up all that available memory. None matched my expectations except Vitals. A breath of fresh air to the UI that conveys all those important vitals that are needed, especially on a bit of a reasonably old machine.

items.paragraph: 现状是自建收藏夹式的轻量网页工具（按新课标重排的地理知识库、交互式周期表、18 类方程式速查）配 GitHub 上可自托管、带记忆自进化的桌面 Agent（vermes），讨论集中在“点开即用、把知识放回情境”这类解法。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的是带长期记忆的“精读—整理—成文”闭环：读文献时自动沉淀可检索的笔记与语言样本，写作卡壳时按论证缺口反查调用，高中侧则把零散考点绑定到具体题型情境而非再做一套题库。

interest_sections.title: AI 任务管理
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是任务管理类界面被功能堆叠拖到关键时刻不可用，而任务数据正被外移成 AI 工具可调用的接口。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 用户最明确的任务是：电脑卡死或资源枯竭时，能立刻调出可用的进程列表、定位并结束吃资源的进程，而不是重启或去命令行敲指令

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 现状是两条线并行：zhihu 上把 Windows 任务管理器功能膨胀 50 多倍、出现幽灵进程、卡时反而更卡当成常态，干脆重启绕过；任务/日程一侧则靠 PingCode 这类可自定义流程字段的团队工具和个人日程 app 盘点来选型，GitHub 上 Feishu-MCP 已把飞书文档与任务包装成 MCP/CLI 供 Cursor、Claude Code 调用。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是把“查询—判断—处置”从越堆越重的 GUI 里拆成最小接口，让 AI 编码工具能通过 MCP/CLI 直接读写任务与进程状态，同时保证系统高负载时这条通道仍然可用。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前做法是在知乎上罗列邮箱验证、黑名单检测等零散工具，或推荐AI邮箱客户端（如WAIMAOINBOAX）辅助英文回复和客户跟进，而GitHub上的mcp_agent_mail则代表用异步协调层管理收件箱和线程的另一条技术思路。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的是把发件前邮箱有效性/黑名单检查、AI英文回复草稿和客户跟进提醒串成一条外贸邮件流水线，并参考mcp_agent_mail的线程化协调方式管理多客户往来。

interest_sections.title: AI 财务管家
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，显示财务从业者对AI的需求正从“减少手工记账”转向“让AI直接做经营分析和风险解释”。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 财务人员需要AI把发票、银行流水、ERP等多源数据自动整合，直接完成对账、凭证生成、结账和异常标记，并能解释利润或现金流变动原因

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 当前讨论集中在推荐微软Copilot、用友好会计、金蝶云星辰/星空、九数云BI等分环节工具，分别做自动对账、凭证生成、税务申报和可视化分析，但跨系统取数仍靠人工，缺少统一入口。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的产品方向是具备自然语言交互的财务智能体，能自主执行“数据采集—关联分析—归因解释—风险预警”闭环，像Copilot解释毛利率下降原因那样直接输出可行动的财务洞察。
